# A route parameter and a root component's state var, reaching one route.
#
# The two arrived from different directions and meet in `newRouteGC`. #215
# hoists a root component's `var` onto the window the component lifts, so the
# route's expression context is scoped to that window or `hits` renders as a
# bare name the emitted Go never declares. But a window's vars are also where
# the checker puts the `{id}` an href declares -- and that one is bound from
# the URL the request arrived on, per request, not per session.
#
# So the window scope has to answer for one and not the other: `hits` is a
# field of the per-session State, `id` is the handler local
# `writeRouteParamBindings` declares. Scoped without that split, `id` came out
# as `s.Id` against a State struct that had no business carrying it -- and it
# compiled, because `routeStateVars` had put the field there too.

sngl generate --lang go --platform html -o out app.sngl

exec go build ./...

# The parameter is the local, the state var is the field.
grep 'id := __r.PathValue\("id"\)' out/server.go
grep 'html.EscapeString\(id\)' out/server.go
grep 's.Hits' out/server.go

# And the parameter is not a field of it.
! grep 's\.Id' out/server.go

-- go.mod --
module rootparam

go 1.24

-- srv/srv.go --
package srv

func Bump(n int) int { return n + 1 }

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import "go:rootparam/srv"
import "sngl:platform/html"

component main ui.root {
    var hits = 0

    ui.window #page(title="t", href="/p/{id}") {
        html.button(innerText="go", @click { hits = srv.Bump(hits) })
        html.span(innerText="{id}")
        html.span(innerText="{hits}")
    }
}
